question: Assuming Gareth Evan's Generality Constraint, if I understand a proposition Fa, should I be able to understand Fx (\forall x)? Assume I understand universal quantification.

4.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Yes, under Evans' Generality Constraint the capacity to grasp Fa already equips one to recombine the same predicate F with any object-term one can think about; once universal quantification is independently understood, nothing further blocks substituting the bound variable for the singular term, yielding grasp of ∀x Fx as a legitimate recombinatory exercise of the same conceptual capacities.

Universal quantification is given as understood, so the same F must be recombinable inside the quantifier to yield ∀x Fx.

(The constraint does not by itself generate new objects of thought, but it does guarantee that an already-understood quantificational frame can be filled by any grasped predicate.)

The constraint requires that mastery of a predicative concept F consists in a general capacity to apply it to any object one can think about, so that if one grasps Fa then one must also be able to entertain Fb, Fc, and so on for any singular term one possesses. Universal quantification is stipulated as already understood, which means the only additional element needed to move from Fa to ∀x Fx is the ability to bind the free variable with the quantifier. Because GC already guarantees recombinability of F with any object-term, nothing further blocks substituting the bound variable for a in the quantified context; the resulting thought ∀x Fx is simply the universal closure of a thought whose constituents one already commands. Thus the constraint is satisfied precisely when one can move from the instance to the generalization.
